version.approval_notes:
OpenPath Firefox extension review notes

Purpose
- Browser companion for managed OpenPath devices in education.
- Explains blocked pages/resources, supports access requests when enabled, provides local allowlist checks through the OpenPath native host, and blocks known Google game surfaces.

Permission rationale
- <all_urls>: evaluates managed navigation/resource requests and applies path, subdomain, Google game, and local Windows dependency-overlay policy across web origins.
- webRequest/webRequestBlocking: detect and apply managed blocked navigation/resource decisions. On Windows, eligible subresource requests are reduced to anchorHost, dependencyHost, and requestType before local native-host validation.
- webNavigation: tracks the top-level anchor host per tab and clears per-tab state on navigation.
- tabs: scopes badge and popup data to the active tab, and redirects already-open tabs to the blocked-page screen when local policy stops allowing their host.
- nativeMessaging: talks only to the local OpenPath native host on the same computer.
- storage: keeps managed config and local runtime state in browser storage.
- clipboardWrite: copies blocked-domain lists only after a user action.

Network/data behavior
- Manifest data collection declares required browsingActivity: managed unblock requests transmit blocked-domain activity and request context to the configured OpenPath service.
- User-initiated access requests verify the install-time browsingActivity permission before sending details to the OpenPath service.
- Google game blocking is local browser policy via webRequest. A Search/Doodles visual guard content script neutralizes detected game widgets, sending only a best-effort local diagnostic to the background runtime.
- Content scripts: a page activity relay, a MAIN-world page-resource observer, and the Google visual guard; page-resource candidates are local.
- Runtime dependency handling is local-only: one persistent native-messaging port sends only anchorHost, dependencyHost, and requestType; the host validates locally and writes exact-host DNS exceptions. An unproven render-critical request is cancelled at its budget (no DNS, no negative) and the tab is reloaded once when the host applies it. A slow call never drops a live port; reconnects need a real disconnect or a failed liveness ping.
- Open-tab reconciliation is local: Firefox polls a local policy stamp and redirects newly-disallowed tabs to the local blocked-page screen.
- - Extension diagnostics are local-only: rate-limited decision events (hosts, types, reasons, ids, ms; no URLs or page content) go over the persistent port to the user's native-host.log.
Firefox Core excludes Android support, remote automatic AJAX/page-resource allowlisting, and live/automatic AMO upload.
- No third-party analytics, advertising, or sale/sharing of browser data is included.

Source review
- Human-readable source is attached; see SOURCE_REVIEW_NOTES.md for rebuild/review notes.

release_notes.en-US:
OpenPath Firefox companion build for managed education devices.

This version includes the blocked-page/request flow, local OpenPath native-host integration, path/subdomain enforcement, local Google games enforcement, Google Search/Doodles visual guard content script, page activity relay, and Windows local exact-host dependency overlays without remote automatic allowlisting or automatic upload. It does not include third-party analytics or telemetry.
